# Species pages: generated by combining FishRadar + FishBase + Wikipedia/Wikidata

We generate the full 196-species page set by combining three external sources via an importer script (`encyclopedia/import_species.py`), not by hand-writing each page. The FishRadar catalog is the authoritative species list and identity; FishBase supplies biological data and family/genus resolution; Wikipedia/Wikidata supplies prose, images, and taxonomy. This ADR records that pipeline so future sessions generate pages the same way without re-negotiating the approach.

## Why combine three sources

The FishRadar catalog is a complete, stable list of 196 sport-fishing species (`data/species.json`, CC BY 4.0), but it only carries identity and fishing-season data. The site schema needs much more: taxonomy (family/genus), physical dimensions, habitat, behavior, a distribution map, an image, and prose. No single source provides all of it, so we combine them:

| Data | Source |
|------|--------|
| Species list, stable id, aliases, saltwater/freshwater, latitude band, season months, conservation flag | **FishRadar** `data/species.json` |
| Family / genus / order / class, distribution coordinates | **Wikidata** (SPARQL over the taxon's parent-taxon chain, P171/P105) |
| Lead prose (extract), page title, hero image, `wikibase_item` | **Wikipedia** (REST `page/summary`) |
| Physical, habitat, behavior detail | **FishBase** when its API is reachable |

## Canonical FishRadar source

- Repo: `https://github.com/linkanlabs-ctrl/fishing-species-catalog`
- File: `data/species.json` — an array of 196 entries.
- Entry shape: `id` (stable kebab-case slug), `scientific` (binomial), `english` (common name), `aliases` (multilingual), `environment` (`saltwater`/`freshwater`), `latRange` `[minLat, maxLat]` signed degrees, `seasonMonths` `[1-12]` Northern Hemisphere, `conservationStatus` (`cites-ii`/`no-retention`/`permit-required`/`vulnerable`/`null`).
- License: CC BY 4.0. We mirror the species list into our own `encyclopedia/data/fish/...` profiles (attribution noted), so the site does not depend on the remote JSON at build time.

## Source-to-profile mapping

| Profile field | From |
|---------------|------|
| `slug` / `id` | FishRadar `id` |
| `taxonomy.scientific_name` | FishRadar `scientific` (also `genus` + `species` split) |
| `taxonomy.common_name` | FishRadar `english` |
| `taxonomy.class/order/family/genus` | Wikidata SPARQL over the taxon's `P171` parent chain, labelled `P105` ranks |
| `taxonomy.aliases` | FishRadar `aliases` |
| `habitat.water_types` | FishRadar `environment` → `[saltwater]` or `[freshwater]` |
| `distribution.regions` | FishRadar `latRange` → latitude markers + generic region prose |
| `angling.season_months` | FishRadar `seasonMonths` |
| `conservation.status` | FishRadar `conservationStatus` (fallback `LC`) |
| `image` | Wikipedia REST `originalimage`, with credit + source link |
| Body prose | Wikipedia REST `extract`, expanded into the standard section structure |
| `physical` / `habitat` / `behavior` detail | FishBase API when reachable; otherwise clear placeholders |

## Field mapping for fish with non-matching schema

The FishRadar catalog includes a few non-fish species of angling interest (e.g. Common octopus, cuttlefish, squid). Their taxonomy still resolves via Wikidata; `class` falls back to their actual phylum/class where not Actinopterygii.

## How to regenerate

```bash
unset ALL_PROXY all_proxy http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY  # repo requires proxyless curl
uv run python3 encyclopedia/import_species.py   # writes all 196 profile .md files
uv run python3 encyclopedia/generate.py          # builds the HTML
```

The importer is idempotent: rerun after editing the FishRadar JSON or schema without destroying hand refinements it leaves untouched.

## Future

If the FishBase API (currently behind a Cloudflare challenge) becomes reachable, wire its physical/habitat/behavior fields into the importer for the fields currently left as placeholders.
